newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ weighs frigate escort for Bougainville leaders.
newsitem.headline: NZ weighs frigate escort for Bougainville leaders.

text.p: New Zealand may send a frigate escort to protect leaders from Papua New Guinea's Bougainville Island when they return home after peace talks here, government officials said on Monday.
New Zealand's Foreign Minister Don McKinnon on Friday made a plea at the end of two weeks of talks for the 70 or so delegates to be allowed to return home unharmed.

Diplomatic sources who attended the talks at Burnham army camp near the city of Christchurch said Wellington was concerned to avoid the repetition of an incident in late 1995 when PNG defence forces ambushed a rebel delegation returning from similar talks in Cairns, Australia.
"A proposal for the return of the Bougainvilleans has gone up to cabinet today and it does involve the use of New Zealand navy ships," a Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade official told Reuters.
According to the Dominion newspaper, the proposal included diverting the frigate Canterbury and the supply ship Endeavour from exercises north of Australia.
A spokeswoman for McKinnon confirmed there was a proposal, but declined to reveal any specific details.

"It is likely it will involve the RNZAF (Royal New Zealand Air Force) and the navy but ... operational details are being worked through, and there's no final plan in place as yet. It is expected they (the Bougainvillean leaders) will leave this week," she said.

Thousands have died in nine years of fighting on Bougainville and leaders of all the main local factions involved, but not the PNG government, on Friday agreed to form a new joint approach to Port Moresby in future negotiations.

The minister, who said he sought to keep PNG leaders informed throughout the talks, said on Friday he had requested that the groups be allowed safe passage to return home, as was the case when they departed.
He also asked "that both sides should now resist any desire to continue the conflict".

McKinnon has pledged to keep up his contact with Port Moresby representatives, and is due to meet them in Kuala Lumpur at the regional forum of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) next week.
"I will encourage the PNG government to see the very positive aspect to and conclusion of the talks," he said.
The Bougainville leaders are due to present the Burnham peace declaration to their people when they return and intend to use it as a base for any future talks with PNG.
